title: How can the teacher split the class into two equal groups?
description: A sports teacher has seventeen students of different heights and wants a shorter group and a taller group. The heights are sorted, the median is found and used to split the class, and the mean is used to guess the students' age.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median has as many values on one side as on the other, so it is a fair place to split a group. Watch for children who split at the mean, which does not give equal groups.

video_script.why: The child can find a median and now uses it to make a decision.
video_script.substitution: Half the students are below the median and half above it.
video_script.payoff_line: Split the class at the median, one hundred and fifteen centimetres.

final_answer.value: Split at the median, 115 cm; mean ≈ 113.53 cm suggests about 6 to 7 years old
final_answer.spoken: split the class at the median, one hundred and fifteen centimetres, and the students are about six to seven years old

maths_rules: 17 values, so the median is the 9th value, 115 cm, with 8 values on each side
5 students are exactly 115 cm: 7 shorter and 5 taller
17 is odd, so two groups cannot be exactly equal: 8 shortest, the middle student set aside, 8 tallest
the 115 cm students are measured more finely to place them
mean 1930 ÷ 17 ≈ 113.53 cm, near the age 6 averages 113.1 and 112.9, a little above
video_script.design: One sorted row of seventeen heights. The ninth is the median, with eight on each side.
open_questions: The age part is taken from the worklist: the book's table of average heights by age (113.1 and 112.9 cm at age 6) is not in the extracted book text, so those two numbers could not be checked.
Seventeen is odd, so two exactly equal groups are impossible. The script splits by position (8, 1, 8) and measures the five students at 115 cm more finely, as the worklist says.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, split the class at the median. Seventeen is odd, so the groups cannot be exactly equal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Put the eight shortest in one group and the eight tallest in the other. The middle student is set aside.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Five students stand at exactly one hundred and fifteen. Measure them more finely to decide their places.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, find the mean to guess the age.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The seventeen heights add up to one thousand nine hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Divided by seventeen, the mean is about one hundred and thirteen point five three centimetres.
